```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

MoFIA fits moderated nonlinear factor analysis (MNLFA) models: factor models in
which item parameters (loadings, thresholds or intercepts, residual variances)
and factor parameters (means, variances, correlations) depend on moderators such
as age or gender. Moderators can be continuous or categorical, and there can be
any number of them. This makes it possible to test measurement invariance and
differential item functioning (DIF) without forming groups.

## Data

The `parabelief` data contain 14 paranormal-belief items, rated from 1
(*definitely not*) to 5 (*definitely*), for 600 Dutch respondents, together
with standardized age and gender (Hoogeveen et al., 2024). Here we analyse the
six items on belief in *unearthly beings*. Their answers are strongly skewed,
so we treat them as ordinal.

```{r}
library(MoFIA)
data(parabelief)
ub <- c("SpiritsGhosts", "GnomesElves", "Aliens", "DevilPossession",
        "Sorcery", "HauntedPlaces")
sapply(parabelief[ub], function(x) round(prop.table(table(x)), 2))
```

## Specifying models

A model is specified with `mofia_model()` and fitted with `mofia()`. By
default, the factor mean and variance are moderated by all moderators, and the
item parameters are not moderated. Moderation of item parameters is added with
`loading_mod` and `threshold_mod`, for example as a vector of item names (these
items, moderated by all moderators).

To compare factor means across the moderators, at least one item must keep
invariant parameters; here `SpiritsGhosts` serves as the anchor. Without an
anchor, a moderated factor mean cannot be told apart from equal threshold
shifts of all items (and a moderated factor variance from equal changes of all
loadings); `mofia_model()` refuses such exactly unidentified models and warns
about weakly identified ones. We fit three nested models:

* **scalar**: no item parameter is moderated;
* **metric**: the thresholds of all items except the anchor are moderated;
* **configural**: in addition, the loadings of all items except the anchor are moderated.

```{r}
others <- setdiff(ub, "SpiritsGhosts")
m_scalar <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"))
m_metric <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                        threshold_mod = others)
m_config <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                        threshold_mod = others, loading_mod = others)
m_metric
```

## Fitting

```{r}
scalar <- mofia(m_scalar)
metric <- mofia(m_metric)
config <- mofia(m_config)
metric
```

`mofia()` uses the logistic link for categorical items by default
(`link = "probit"` is also available). The factors are integrated out by
adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature. A fit counts as converged when the
information matrix is positive definite (a maximum, not a saddle point, and an
identified model) and the Newton decrement, the log-likelihood gain still
available from one more Newton step, is negligible. Otherwise no standard errors
or tests are reported.

## Comparing models

`anova()` compares nested models with likelihood-ratio tests, by default with
the Satorra-Bentler scaling correction for robust (MLR) estimation:

```{r}
anova(scalar, metric, config)
```

Moderating the thresholds improves the fit clearly, so at least some items show
threshold DIF. Moderating the loadings does not improve it further, so the
loadings can be treated as invariant.

A Wald test checks DIF for a single item. The tested parameters can be named
directly or selected with a regular expression:

```{r}
mofia_wald(metric, "^beta\\[DevilPossession,", regex = TRUE)
```

## Screening all items at once: score tests

Instead of fitting one model per item, `mofia_score_test()` tests every
moderation effect that a fitted model does not contain, from that one fit
(like modification indices). Here we screen the scalar model; `by = "item"`
tests each item's threshold or loading moderation jointly over both moderators:

```{r}
screen <- mofia_score_test(scalar, by = "item")
screen[, c("test", "df", "statistic", "p", "p_adj")]
```

The robust statistics flag threshold DIF for Aliens, DevilPossession and
SpiritsGhosts (Holm-adjusted *p* < .05) and no loading DIF, in line with the
model comparisons above. SpiritsGhosts, the anchor of the models above, is
flagged too. Tests against a scalar model are relative to the other items, and
choosing anchors is a known difficulty of DIF analysis. The item with the
weakest evidence for DIF (here GnomesElves) is a natural candidate for a
sensitivity analysis with another anchor, but this is a heuristic: choosing
anchors from the same data and then testing on these data is post-selection
inference, and the Holm adjustment covers only the screen itself. Substantive
arguments or independent data are the better basis for anchors.

## Parameter estimates

`summary()` prints all estimates, grouped by parameter type. The table can also
be used directly:

```{r}
est <- summary(metric)$coefficients
est[est$type %in% c("beta", "gamma", "delta"), c("estimate", "se", "z", "p")]
```

`gamma` parameters are the moderation effects on the factor mean, and `delta`
parameters on the log factor variance. Both are on the scale of the baseline
factor (mean 0 and variance 1 for a person with all moderators at 0). `beta`
parameters shift all thresholds of an item. Standard errors are robust (MLR) by
default, a sandwich with the exact observed information; `summary(fit, se =
"ML")` and `vcov(fit, se = "ML")` give the model-based ones. The robust
correction protects the standard errors against misspecified distributions; it
does not make a misspecified moderation effect the quantity of scientific
interest.

## Plots, factor scores and predictions

`plot()` shows how the factor mean and SD change with a moderator, how
moderated loadings change, or item response functions at several moderator
values (DIF shows as curves that differ):

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
plot(metric, "factors", moderator = "Age")
plot(metric, "items", moderator = "Male", items = c("DevilPossession", "Aliens"))
```

`mofia_scores()` gives EAP factor scores with posterior SDs (conditional on
the estimated parameters, so they do not include estimation uncertainty), and
`predict()` gives model-implied category probabilities or expected item scores
for chosen moderator values. Plot bands are pointwise:

```{r}
head(mofia_scores(metric), 3)
predict(metric, newdata = data.frame(Age = c(-1, 1), Male = c(0, 1)))
```

## Continuous items

Items can also be treated as continuous (normal), with log-linearly moderated
residual variances:

```{r}
m_cont <- mofia_model(parabelief, items = ub, moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                      threshold_mod = others, continuous = ub)
cont <- mofia(m_cont)
cont$scaling
```

The robust scaling correction factor is well above 1, a sign that the
normal model does not fit these skewed items well. The ordinal model's factor is
close to 1 (`metric$scaling`). Ordinal and continuous items can also be mixed
in one model.

## Formulas and model syntax

Moderators can also be given as a formula. Factor variables are dummy-coded,
and interactions and transformations are allowed; `standardize = TRUE` turns
continuous moderators into z-scores (new data for `predict()` and plots stay
on the original scale). The loading pattern can be written in lavaan style:

```{r}
m_f <- mofia_model(parabelief, loadings = "UB =~ SpiritsGhosts + GnomesElves + Aliens +
                                           DevilPossession + Sorcery + HauntedPlaces",
                   moderators = ~ Age * Male, standardize = TRUE)
m_f$moderators
```

## More than one factor

For several factors, give the loading pattern as a named list or as model
syntax. With two
factors, the factor correlation can be moderated as well (`cor_mod`), on the
Fisher-z scale. This model is not run here because it takes somewhat longer:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
eha <- c("HealingHands", "LifeCoursePossessions", "Graphology", "Dowsing",
         "MindReading", "Willpower", "SeeingFuture", "SeeingEvents")
m2 <- mofia_model(parabelief, loadings = list(EHA = eha, UB = ub),
                  moderators = c("Age", "Male"),
                  threshold_mod = TRUE, mean_mod = FALSE, cor_mod = TRUE)
fit2 <- mofia(m2, threads = 4)
```

With three or more factors, moderated correlations are refused by default:
pairwise moderated correlations need not form a valid correlation matrix for all
moderator values, and this case is not yet methodologically established.
